text: A Mermaid sequenceDiagram, with short notes, covering login (success, bad credentials and lockout), a request for a protected page, and logout.
An unknown email and a wrong password get the identical HTTP 401 response with "Invalid email or password".

After 5 failed attempts for an email within any 10-minute period, logins for that email are refused with HTTP 429 for 15 minutes without checking the password, and a successful login clears the count.
Every successful login issues a new random session ID, destroys any session the incoming cookie pointed to, and redirects to /dashboard.
The cookie carries only the opaque session ID and is HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax.
Each protected request is checked on the server against a 30-minute sliding idle limit and a 12-hour absolute limit. An invalid session gets its cookie cleared and a redirect to /login.
Logout destroys the server-side session before replying, clears the cookie, redirects to /login, and behaves the same when no session exists.
The artifact states where sessions and failure counts are stored, outside process memory, so both instances see the same state.
